name: mq_open
synopsis: mqd_t mq_open(const char *name, int oflag, mode_t mode, struct mq_attr *attr);
description: mq_open() creates a new POSIX message queue or opens an existing queue. The queue is identified by name, and the oflag argument specifies flags that control the operation.

parameters.name: name
parameters.description: The name of the message queue.

parameters.name: oflag
parameters.description: Flags that control the operation of the call, such as O_RDONLY, O_WRONLY, O_RDWR, and optional flags like O_CLOEXEC or O_CREAT.

parameters.name: mode
parameters.description: Permissions to be placed on the new queue if O_CREAT is specified.

parameters.name: attr
parameters.description: Pointer to attributes specifying the maximum number of messages and message size for the new queue if O_CREAT is specified.

return_value.success: Returns a message queue descriptor for use by other message queue functions
return_value.failure: Returns (mqd_t)-1 on error, with errno set to indicate the error

errors.description: The queue exists, but the caller does not have permission to open it in the specified mode.
name contained more than one slash.
Both O_CREAT and O_EXCL were specified in oflag, but a queue with this name already exists.
name doesn’t follow the required format, or O_CREAT was specified with invalid attr values.
The per-process limit on the number of open file and message queue descriptors has been reached.
The system-wide limit on the total number of open files and message queues has been reached.
The O_CREAT flag was not specified, and no queue with this name exists.
Insufficient space for the creation of a new message queue.

bugs: Before Linux 2.6.14, the process umask was not applied to the permissions specified in mode.
